note: Frozen BEFORE any session of the ESL stage-1 study. Per student and form: v1 = post-test, v2 = parallel "consistency check" form (given after an unrelated filler task; it does not measure memory over days). 4 controlled + 2 free-production + 2 next-level items each. Controlled and next-level items are scored deterministically (exact match of the missing word, benchmark/scoring.ts); free-production items are scored by blind scorer agents with the rubric in `freeRubric`. No item appears in any lesson exercise (eslStudy.ts ready). Tutors never see these items.

freeRubric.articles: Look ONLY at articles. A sentence is correct if it contains at least one singular countable noun that needs an article and EVERY article in it is right: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound, the for something known or already mentioned, no article where English uses none. A missing article before a singular countable noun, a wrong a/an, or the used where a/an is needed makes the sentence wrong. A sentence with no noun that needs an article is wrong (the form was not used). Ignore every other error.
freeRubric.copula: Look ONLY at am, is and are. A sentence is correct if it has at least one present-tense statement with be (am, is or are) and every be-verb is present, correct for its subject (I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are), and none is left out where English needs it. A missing be-verb ("She tired"), a wrong form ("They is"), or is added before another main verb ("He is play") makes the sentence wrong. A sentence with no present be-statement is wrong (the form was not used). Ignore every other error.
freeRubric.thirdS: Look ONLY at the present simple with he, she, it or a singular name. A sentence is correct if it has at least one present-simple verb with a third person singular subject and EVERY such verb has the correct -s, -es or -ies ending (watches, studies, goes, plays), spelled correctly. A base verb after he/she/it ("She like tea"), a wrong ending ("watchs"), or an -s added after I, you, we or they makes the sentence wrong. A sentence with no third-person-singular present verb is wrong (the form was not used). Ignore every other error.
